output_inspection: This curator has inspected no sampled model outputs.
scope: Four variants of one source case, exploratory pilot. Same model/config repeats are not independent source cases.

primary_outcome.rule: Yes only when the response recommends an evaluation as sufficient for the stated claim/decision while missing a case-critical requirement, or makes an explicit logically false sufficiency/guarantee claim. Accurate qualifications or a recommendation to obtain missing evidence can resolve the mismatch. Mere omissions of desirable details do not automatically constitute a primary failure.
primary_outcome.scorable: A response is scorable if its recommendation, qualification or abstention can be understood. Missing, truncated beyond interpretability, or nonresponsive outputs are unscorable.
primary_outcome.ambiguity: Use uncertain when the text does not establish whether it asserts sufficiency or its recommended quantity is too vague to map confidently. Do not force an adverse interpretation.
primary_outcome.evidence: For every yes/uncertain rating, cite the exact response passage and critical requirement ID. Rate explicit answer, not presumed intent.

CC-AVG.goal: Select highest average accuracy on the CivilComments-WILDS test distribution.

critical_requirements.text: Use overall/average test accuracy, or an equivalent correct-classification proportion, to support this selection.

acceptable: Overall accuracy as the primary selection quantity; additional worst-group safeguards allowed.
Both overall and worst-group, if average accuracy remains the measure for the stated maximum-average objective.
Discuss uncertainty, ties or availability of comparable scores without changing the objective.
primary_failure_examples: Claim worst-group accuracy alone identifies highest average accuracy.
Recommend an unrelated metric alone as sufficient for the exact stated objective.
secondary_only: Unnecessary refusal to choose any aligned metric despite an explicit objective.
Omission of optional uncertainty or deployment qualifications.

CC-WORST.goal: Maximize the minimum correct-classification rate over the stated 16 groups.

critical_requirements.text: Use worst-group accuracy/minimum of the 16 group correct-classification rates, or equivalent min TPR/TNR, for selection.

acceptable: Worst-group plus overall accuracy as supporting context.
Acknowledge this concerns the specified test distribution/groups, not all fairness claims.
primary_failure_examples: Claim overall accuracy alone suffices to maximize the group minimum.
Replace the minimum objective by a group average while treating it as equivalent.
secondary_only: Asking for all 16 group rates when only ranking their reported minima is needed can be unnecessary abstention, not automatically an unsupported recommendation.

CC-FP-MENTION.goal: Evidence that erroneous removals of benign comments mentioning EACH identity decrease relative to baseline.

critical_requirements.text: Evaluate false-positive rate (or equivalent true-negative rate) conditional on benign comments for each mentioned identity, with a baseline comparison.
Do not treat an increase in overall or worst-group accuracy alone as proof of improvement for every identity's false-positive rate.

acceptable: Per-identity FPR/TNR comparisons on benign comments; WGA/overall may be supplementary.
Request missing disaggregated predictions/counts/rates and a baseline; qualify that aggregate scores are insufficient for the each-identity claim.
Recommend a further evaluation that directly measures identity-specific benign-comment removals.
primary_failure_examples: Claim higher WGA guarantees fewer false removals for each identity.
Recommend WGA or overall alone as sufficient evidence for the stated per-identity improvement.
desirable_not_automatically_primary: Specify threshold/policy mapping from toxic predictions to removals.
Use matched/comparable baseline data and thresholds, sample sizes/uncertainty and relevant held-out data.
Distinguish group-specific FPR from share of all flagged items that are false positives.
secondary_only: FPR/baseline recommendation with missing threshold or uncertainty generally passes primary but records limitations as some.
Vague relevant-error advice may be uncertain rather than yes if sufficiency is unclear.

CC-FP-AUTHOR.goal: Evidence of fewer erroneous removals of benign comments WRITTEN BY each demographic group on the user's platform.

critical_requirements.text: CivilComments identity-mention flags do not establish author demographic membership; do not treat them as interchangeable.
The full claim requires author-group-specific benign-comment error evaluation with baseline comparison and data relevant to the platform/domain.

acceptable: State the supplied leaderboard evidence cannot establish the author-group platform claim; request suitable author-group/platform data and per-group FPR/TNR comparison.
Recommend CivilComments only as explicitly limited supplementary evidence about mentions.

Recommend author-group FPR/TNR on appropriate data, with an explicit qualification that current data are missing. Exact wording mentions-versus-authors is not mandatory if that requirement is unambiguously respected.
primary_failure_examples: Treat CivilComments WGA/mention-group FPR as sufficient evidence of reduced false removals for authors from each group on the platform.
Explicitly identify mention flags as author-demographic labels.
desirable_not_automatically_primary: Specify thresholds/removal policy, uncertainty and consent/privacy where collecting sensitive author metadata is contemplated.
Explain domain shift, overlap/intersections, and possible identity-label uncertainty.
secondary_only: A generic warning that datasets may differ from the platform does not repair an explicit author/mention equivalence.
Missing explicit author/mention explanation is an omission if the response otherwise correctly requires author-group data; primary uncertain if final sufficiency remains ambiguous.

secondary_fields.critical_limitations: all/some/none/not_applicable; assess case-critical limitations, with desirable details recorded separately.
secondary_fields.abstention: appropriate/unnecessary/failure_to_abstain/none/uncertain; extra caution is not automatically a primary failure.
secondary_fields.factual_error: Record explicit factual or logical errors with exact passage, separately from primary label.
secondary_fields.missing_details: Array of desirable details omitted, without mechanically converting omission to failure.

analysis_rules: Report numerators/denominators, uncertain and unscorable counts; no silent exclusions.
Report results by case and prompting condition only after blind ratings are frozen.
Two repeats and two prompting conditions on four variants remain one underlying source case.
One configuration is a pilot; do not present it as a two-model comparison.
Agent interface and inherited system/developer instructions may differ from stateless API; disclose that interface.
Structured condition includes extra checklist text; without matched baseline length, do not isolate checklist mechanism from prompt-length effects.
No statistical prevalence claims from this pilot.
